findings.evidence: TIMESTAMP literal is parsed at build/compile time and cached in the builtin: `pkg/expression/builtin_time.go:4693` calls `types.ParseTime(ctx.GetEvalCtx().TypeCtx(), ...)` and `pkg/expression/builtin_time.go:4738` returns the stored `b.tm` without consulting runtime ctx. When the input contains an explicit offset, parsing converts into the session time zone location: `pkg/types/time.go:1186` enters `hasTZ` branch and `pkg/types/time.go:1213` does `t1 = t1.In(ctx.Location())`. Plan cache key only hashes the *current* time zone offset, not the time zone identity/rules: `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_utils.go:293` computes `timezoneOffset` via `time.Now().In(vars.TimeZone).Zone()` and `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_utils.go:323` hashes it. Named time zones (with DST rules) are supported: `pkg/util/timeutil/time_zone.go:232` uses `time.LoadLocation(s)`.
findings.fix: Make TIMESTAMP literal with explicit offset re-evaluate under the execution session’s `TypeCtx` (e.g., store the original string in the builtin and parse in `evalTime`), OR strengthen plan-cache keying to include the session `time_zone` identity (not just current offset), OR conservatively mark statements containing `TIMESTAMP '...±HH:MM'` as uncacheable for plan cache.
findings.impact: Under prepared/non-prepared/instance plan cache, changing `@@time_zone` between two different locations that share the same *current* offset (e.g., a DST zone vs a fixed offset) can reuse a cached plan and return a silently wrong TIMESTAMP-literal value for dates where the zone’s offset differs (DST vs standard time). This can affect query results and also DML correctness if such literals are used in writes.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: timestamp-literal still parses/caches `tm` at build time in `pkg/expression/builtin_time.go`, and plan-cache keying still uses `time.Now().In(vars.TimeZone).Zone()` offset in `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_utils.go`; no follow-up change found that would re-evaluate timestamp literals per execution or hash full time zone identity.
findings.verify: Repro under plan cache: 1) enable prepared/instance plan cache; 2) `SET @@time_zone='America/New_York'; PREPARE s FROM "SELECT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 14:00:00+01:00'"; EXECUTE s;` 3) `SET @@time_zone='-04:00'; EXECUTE s;` Expected second result to differ (NY in 2024-01-01 is -05:00, fixed -04:00 differs); if it stays the same, cached plan baked the old conversion.
findings.what: Plan-cache correctness risk: TIMESTAMP literals with explicit `±HH:MM` offsets are converted into the session time zone at expression build time and stored as a constant builtin value, but plan cache key only captures the current time zone offset (not the full zone identity/rules). Cached plans can therefore be reused across different `@@time_zone` settings with the same current offset, yielding wrong literal values (especially with DST-capable named zones).

subject: expression: Timestamp literal with time zone offset (#57845)
summary: Updates TIMESTAMP-literal format validation to accept `±HH:MM` offsets and switches format-mismatch errors to `ErrWrongValue2` (1525). Main High risk: timestamp literals with offsets are converted to session time zone at build time and cached, which can become stale/incorrect when a cached plan is reused under a different `@@time_zone` that shares the same current offset (DST vs fixed-offset scenarios).
